angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 210,519 km at 27.83 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 35.9298 +/- 0.0253 mas (same row, RUWE 1.30): 27.83 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.3026 +/- 0.0095 solar radii from Luque et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of G 9-40 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A.154L/abstract): 210,519 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.2952 +/- 0.0136 solar masses from Luque et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of G 9-40 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A.154L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3395 +/- 51 K from Luque et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of G 9-40 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A.154L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
